free.title: VERVE AT 70: FREE JAZZ IN THE PARK
free.caption:
FREE TONIGHT · CENTRAL PARK

Samara Joy and Christian McBride play a free SummerStage show tonight in Central Park - 17 Grammys on one stage for exactly zero dollars.

Verve Records turns 70 this year, and the label that gave the world Ella Fitzgerald, Stan Getz and Oscar Peterson gets a hometown salute: Bronx-born Samara Joy sings, bass giant Christian McBride swings, and Mei Semones reworks Getz/Gilberto for 2026. Sparklmami spins between sets.

Tip: a picnic blanket beats a folding chair here - you can slide closer as the lawn shuffles.

food.title: UNION SQUARE GREENMARKET AT PEAK HARVEST
food.caption:
NYC FOOD · UNION SQUARE

The Union Square Greenmarket is peaking right now - early September is when the best of the regional harvest lands in the middle of Manhattan.

This is the flagship of the city's greenmarket system, running four days a week since 1976. Come at opening and you will be shopping next to restaurant chefs doing their morning buy; come at noon and it is a full-blown scene, with buskers working the park edge.

Tip: ask vendors for 'seconds' - blemished heirlooms cost less and taste identical in a sauce.

Tag the friend who owns 14 tote bags.

art.title: 6 SECRETS OF THE NYC SUBWAY
art.caption:
HIDDEN GEM · NYC SUBWAY

The subway you ride every day is secretly a museum - ghost stations, hidden artworks and doors that lead somewhere strange, all covered by one $2.90 swipe.

The City Hall station on the cards opened in 1904 as the system's crown jewel, with Guastavino tile and brass chandeliers, and closed in 1945 when its curved platform could no longer fit longer trains. The tunnel movie near DeKalb was built by filmmaker Bill Brand in 1980 and works like a giant zoetrope - your train is the projector.

All six secrets, with lines and stops, are on the cards.
